assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski and Crooks relations show that the second law holds in a precise exact form for small, fluctuating, far-from-equilibrium systems. Stochastic thermodynamics defines work, heat and entropy along single trajectories and now underlies the analysis of molecular machines, single-molecule pulling experiments, colloids and nanodevices. The idea is original, conceptually clean and widely used, and fits the stochastic-process tradition I work in.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss (1993) gave the first fluctuation theorem and Evans and Searles developed it; Jarzynski (1997) gave the nonequilibrium work relation; Crooks (1999) the detailed fluctuation relation; Seifert built the trajectory-level thermodynamic framework. Four credited names but three places: I pick Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert, leaving Crooks as a hard omission whose contribution is close to Jarzynski's.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is strong and independent (RNA hairpin pulling by Liphardt et al., Collin et al., colloidal and electronic single-electron experiments), and the interpretation has been stable for over two decades. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Evans, Jarzynski, Crooks and Seifert is genuinely contestable and any three-person choice omits a major contributor.
I have not independently verified the details of the experimental confirmations or priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Halperin-Nelson-Young theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting predicts a two-step melting via a hexatic phase with quasi-long-range orientational order, driven by unbinding of dislocations and disclinations. It is a landmark of statistical mechanics of ordered phases and topological defects, with applications from colloids to superconducting vortex lattices and Langmuir films.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) are the decisive theory papers, building on Kosterlitz and Thouless, who were already recognised in 2016. The three-person credit is natural and clean.
assessment.maturity: The hexatic phase has been seen experimentally in colloidal and other 2D systems, and simulation debates about the first-order versus continuous nature of melting were largely resolved with the picture that system details matter. Timely given the 2016 prize, if late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently separate from the 2016 Kosterlitz-Thouless-Haldane prize.
Experimental and numerical evidence for the transition scenario is system-dependent, and I have not verified the latest details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory of flocking show that self-propelled agents with alignment interactions develop long-range order in two dimensions, circumventing the Mermin-Wagner theorem, with giant number fluctuations and new universality classes. This founded a large part of active-matter physics and connects to biological collective motion.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek et al. (1995) introduced the minimal model; Toner and Tu (1995, 1998) gave the continuum theory and renormalisation-group analysis. Tu's role is real but secondary to Toner's in the theory; the credit is reasonably clear for the three.
assessment.maturity: Many experiments on bacteria, colloidal rollers, vibrated granular matter and bird flocks support the qualitative picture, and exponent predictions have been tested numerically. The field is mature in theory but some quantitative predictions remain debated.
uncertainties: Quantitative agreement of exponents with experiment in real animal groups is limited.
Whether committee prefers active matter as a whole instead of this narrower candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory solves lattice models of strongly correlated electrons exactly in infinite dimensions by mapping them to a quantum impurity problem, giving a controlled description of the Mott transition and correlated metals. Combined with density functional theory it became a standard tool in materials physics. The impact is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt (1989) introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar (1992) the impurity mapping, and Georges, Kotliar, Krauth and Rozenberg's 1996 review consolidated it. Metzner and Müller-Hartmann are not credited here, so the offered trio is plausible but leaves out Metzner.
assessment.maturity: Well established and confirmed by comparisons with cold-atom and materials experiments; the method continues to be extended (cluster extensions, DFT+DMFT). Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Walter Metzner and others in the early development.
Accuracy limits in finite dimensions and for spatial correlations, and whether it is seen as method versus discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical discovery that in two dimensions particles can have fractional exchange statistics interpolating between bosons and fermions is a conceptual change of the spin-statistics picture and the base of topological quantum matter, fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles and proposals for topological quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim (1977) first identified the possibility; Wilczek (1982) named anyons and developed their physics. Wilczek is already a laureate (2004, for a different discovery) and not necessary; I propose Leinaas and Myrheim as the priority-holders, a fair configuration that preserves the original idea. There is a risk the committee prefers to couple the theory to experimental demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: Experimental support from fractional quantum Hall interferometry and collider experiments (2020 onwards) is now reasonably independent, though the interpretation of such experiments still involves debate. Timely, with the experimental side maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental demonstrations are mature enough, and whether they should be paired with this theory.
Priority and credit between Leinaas-Myrheim and Wilczek, and possible earlier or parallel work I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed trapped-ion quantum gates (1995) and cold-atom quantum simulation in optical lattices, which seeded two experimental platforms for quantum computing and simulation. The originality and impact are very large, although the cold-atom part overlaps with several other candidates.
assessment.attribution: The two-person credit is clean and well supported: the same pair proposed the ion-trap gate and, with Jaksch et al., the Bose-Hubbard optical-lattice scheme. Experimental realisation belongs to others such as Wineland, Blatt and Bloch, so a theory-only prize is plausible but the experiments are part of the story.
assessment.maturity: Both platforms have been confirmed by many independent groups over three decades and are now scaling up. Timely, although the 2012 and 2025 prizes touched neighbouring areas.
uncertainties: Overlap with other candidates on the list (trapped-ion quantum computing, optical lattices) and the question of how best to cut this area.
I have not verified the extent of the overlap with recent prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape theory with its funnel picture, using spin-glass ideas, explains how proteins fold quickly through a minimally frustrated landscape and resolves Levinthal's paradox. It is a physical theory of a central biological problem, of the type that connects disordered-systems statistical physics to biology, and it informs structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) introduced the spin-glass-inspired approach; Onuchic, Wolynes and collaborators developed funnels and the principle of minimal frustration; Dill contributed hydrophobic collapse and lattice models. Choosing two of three is a judgement call; Dill is a serious omission.
assessment.maturity: Supported by many folding experiments and by coarse-grained simulations, but practical structure prediction was achieved by machine learning (recognised in the 2024 chemistry prize), so the relative scientific weight is debated. Recognition would be timely but may be seen as more chemistry or biophysics than physics.
uncertainties: Whether the physics committee would regard this as within its scope or as belonging to chemistry.
Quantitative predictive power of the landscape theory is difficult for me to assess without more evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moiré quantum materials with tunable strongly correlated physics, a rich platform for many-body theory.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) made the theoretical prediction; Cao, Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (2018) the discovery. The three-name configuration is natural, although Cao's role as first author and other experimental groups contribute to the credit question.
assessment.maturity: Rapid independent confirmation across many groups and variants, but the mechanism of superconductivity and some correlated states remain debated, and the field is still young. Possibly somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for the experimental discovery beyond the senior author, and field maturity.
